claims.nodeLabel: Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP)
claims.text: DIA Talking Paper U-973-09 states the RFP broke the work into twelve technical areas: Lift; Propulsion; Control; Armament (radio-frequency and directed-energy weapons); Spatial/temporal Translation; Signature Reduction; Materials; Configuration/structure; Power Generation; Human Effects (of advanced tech on operators); Human Interface (i.e. pilot controls); Technology Integration.

DIA Talking Paper: 'Senator Reid has a deep interest in the potential threat posed by unconventional aerospace technologies; that is, technologies that are a radical departure to those used in current advanced aerospace vehicles. He is interested in what technological "leaps" are feasible and their implications to US national defense.'

edges.label: 24 June 2009 Reid SAP request refused by the Deputy Secretary
edges.note: 'On 24 June 2009, Senator Reid sent a letter to then Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting that AAWSAP/AATIP be made a DoD Special Access Program. Deputy Secretary Lynn declined to do so based on the recommendation of then-Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, James R. Clapper, Jr., that such a designation was not justified.'
